body:

[//]: # "
    # PR Title
    We use the title to create changelog automatically and therefore only allow specific prefixes
    - break:    to indicate a breaking change, this supersedes any of the other types
    - feat:     to indicate new features or checks
    - fix:      to indicate a bugfix or handling of edge cases of existing checks
    - docs:     to indicate an update to our documentation
    - chore:    to indicate adjustments to workflow files or dependency updates
    - platform: to indicate a change needed for the platform
    Each prefix should be accompanied by a scope that specifies the targeted framework. If uncertain, use 'general'.
    #    
    Allowed prefixs:
    ansible|argo|arm|azure|bicep|bitbucket|circleci|cloudformation|dockerfile|github|gha|gitlab|helm|kubernetes|kustomize|openapi|sast|sca|secrets|serverless|terraform|general|graph|terraform_plan|terraform_json
    #
    ex.
    feat(terraform): add CKV_AWS_123 to ensure that VPC Endpoint Service is configured for Manual Acceptance
"

## Description

When scanning Terraform JSON with `--framework terraform_json`, and that json contains a list, but does not contain a tab (just spaces), Checkov crashes with:

```
[MainThread  ] [ERROR]  Failed to invoke function /home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/common/runners/runner_registry._parallel_run with (<checkov.terraform_json.runner.TerraformJsonRunner object at 0xffff8aaa96f0>, '/home/student/Documents/checkov/repo2', ['/tmp/tmpjhwzsu5i'], None, <checkov.runner_filter.RunnerFilter object at 0xffff8aac51e0>, True, None)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/common/parallelizer/parallel_runner.py", line 72, in func_wrapper
    result = original_func(*item)
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/common/runners/runner_registry.py", line 836, in _parallel_run
    report = runner.run(
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/terraform_json/runner.py", line 87, in run
    self.definitions, self.definitions_raw, parsing_errors = create_definitions(file_paths)
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/terraform_json/utils.py", line 59, in create_definitions
    template, file_lines = parse(file_path)
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/terraform_json/parser.py", line 32, in parse
    template, template_lines = loads(file_path=file_path)
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/terraform_json/parser.py", line 77, in loads
    template = prepare_definition(template)
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/terraform_json/parser.py", line 89, in prepare_definition
    definition_new[block_type] = handle_block_type(block_type=block_type, blocks=blocks)
  File "/home/student/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/checkov/terraform_json/parser.py", line 97, in handle_block_type
    for block_name, config in blocks.items():
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items'
```

I believe order of operations is at fault here https://github.com/bridgecrewio/checkov/blob/main/checkov/terraform_json/parser.py#L43 where only if yaml parsing fails (tab present) will it execute json_parse, allowing the dict to populate as expected by handle_block_type() - https://github.com/bridgecrewio/checkov/blob/main/checkov/terraform_json/parser.py#L97

To reproduce:

Fails:
```json
{
    "provider": [
        {
            "aws": {
                "region": "us-west-2",
                "profile": null
            }
        }
    ]
}
```
Works:
```json
{
    "provider": [
	    {
            "aws": {
                "region": "us-west-2",
                "profile": null
            }
        }
    ]
}
```


Fixes # (issue)
- Add _normalize_provider_blocks_list() in checkov/terraform_json/parser.py to convert provider blocks that arrive as a list of dicts into the dict-of-lists shape handle_block_type() already expects.
- Update prepare_definition() so that when block_type == BlockType.PROVIDER and blocks is a list, it normalizes via _normalize_provider_blocks_list() before calling handle_block_type().
- Add a defensive guard in handle_block_type() so that if blocks is still a list for any reason, we log a debug message and return an empty result instead of raising an AttributeError.


## Checklist:

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my feature, policy, or fix is effective and works
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally with my changes

author: copilot
body:
Adds complete Terraform infrastructure for Azure Virtual Machine Scale Set with credentials stored securely in Terraform Cloud.

### Infrastructure Resources (`main.tf`)
- Resource Group, VNet, Subnet, NSG (HTTP/HTTPS inbound)
- Standard SKU Load Balancer with health probe
- Windows VMSS running Windows Server 2022 Datacenter Azure Edition
- Default region: West US 2

### Configuration
- **`backend.tf`** - Terraform Cloud workspace for remote state and credential storage
- **`variables.tf`** - Input variables with password validation (min 12 chars)
- **`outputs.tf`** - Resource IDs and load balancer public IP
- **`providers.tf`** - Azure provider ~> 3.0

### Terraform Cloud Setup
Azure credentials configured as environment variables in the workspace:
```
ARM_CLIENT_ID, ARM_CLIENT_SECRET, ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, ARM_TENANT_ID
```

Update `backend.tf` organization name before use:
```hcl
terraform {
  cloud {
    organization = "your-organization-name"  # <-- customize
    workspaces { name = "az-vmss-workspace" }
  }
}
```

author: prk4224
body:
# [Refactor] 게시글 목록 조회 API 성능 최적화

## 📌 작업 내용
- [ ] 기능 구현
- [ ] 버그 수정
- [x] 리팩토링

## 🔎 상세 내용

### 성능 최적화 작업

게시글 목록 조회 API(`GET /api/v1/community/posts`)의 성능을 최적화하여 N+1 문제를 해결하고 쿼리 수를 대폭 감소시켰습니다.

### 주요 변경 사항

#### 1. 2단계 쿼리 방식으로 페이징 정확성 개선

**문제점**
- `LEFT JOIN FETCH p.images`를 사용할 때, Post 1개에 Image N개가 있으면 JOIN 결과가 N행이 됩니다.
- `Pageable`의 limit이 JOIN 결과 행 수를 기준으로 적용되어 예상보다 적은 수의 Post가 반환될 수 있습니다.
- 예: limit=10으로 설정했지만, Post 1개에 Image 10개가 있으면 실제로는 Post 1개만 반환됨

**해결 방법**
- **1단계**: Post ID만 먼저 조회 (페이징 정상 동작)
- **2단계**: ID 목록으로 Post + user + category를 fetch join
- **3단계**: images는 Batch Fetching으로 자동 로딩

**변경된 Repository 메서드**
// Post ID만 조회
List<Long> findPostIdsForCursor(...);

// ID 목록으로 Post 엔티티 조회
List<CommunityPost> findPostsByIds(List<Long> ids);#### 2. 댓글 수 조회 최적화 (N+1 문제 해결)

**변경 전**
// 각 postId마다 개별 쿼리 실행 (N번의 쿼리)
List<Long> commentCounts = limitedIds.stream()
    .map(communityPostRepository::countActiveCommentsByPostId)
    .toList();**변경 후**
// 한 번의 쿼리로 모든 댓글 수 조회
List<Object[]> commentCountResults = communityPostRepository.countActiveCommentsByPostIds(limitedIds);
Map<Long, Long> commentCountMap = ...;**추가된 Repository 메서드**
@Query("""
    SELECT c.post.id, COUNT(c) 
    FROM PostComment c 
    WHERE c.post.id IN :postIds AND c.active = true 
    GROUP BY c.post.id
    """)
List<Object[]> countActiveCommentsByPostIds(@Param("postIds") List<Long> postIds);#### 3. 좋아요 여부 조회 최적화 (N+1 문제 해결)

**변경 전**
// 각 postId마다 개별 쿼리 실행 (N번의 쿼리)
List<Boolean> likedStatuses = limitedIds.stream()
    .map(postId -> postLikeRepository.existsByPostIdAndUserId(postId, userId))
    .toList();**변경 후**
// 한 번의 쿼리로 모든 좋아요 여부 조회
Set<Long> likedPostIds = postLikeRepository.findLikedPostIdsByPostIdsAndUserId(limitedIds, userId);**추가된 Repository 메서드**a
@Query("SELECT l.post.id FROM PostLike l WHERE l.post.id IN :postIds AND l.user.id = :userId")
List<Long> findLikedPostIdsByPostIdsAndUserId(@Param("postIds") List<Long> postIds, @Param("userId") Long userId);#### 4. Batch Fetching 적용

**Entity 변경**
- `CommunityPost` 엔티티의 `images` 컬렉션에 `@BatchSize(size = 100)` 추가

**설정 변경**
- `application.yml`에 `hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size: 100` 추가

**효과**
- images를 별도로 fetch join하지 않아도 `@BatchSize`로 인해 한 번의 쿼리로 모든 images 로딩됨
- N+1 문제 없이 효율적으로 컬렉션 로딩

#### 5. 테스트 코드 수정

모든 `getPosts` 관련 테스트를 최적화된 코드에 맞게 수정:
- `findActivePostsWithCursor` → `findActivePostIdsForCursor` + `findPostsByIds`
- `countActiveCommentsByPostId` → `countActiveCommentsByPostIds`
- `existsByPostIdAndUserId` → `findLikedPostIdsByPostIdsAndUserId`

### 수정된 파일

1. **`CommunityPostRepository.java`**
   - `findPostIdsForCursor`: Post ID만 조회하는 메서드 추가
   - `findPostsByIds`: ID 목록으로 Post 엔티티 조회하는 메서드 추가
   - `countActiveCommentsByPostIds`: 댓글 수 일괄 조회 메서드 추가

2. **`PostLikeRepository.java`**
   - `findLikedPostIdsByPostIdsAndUserId`: 좋아요 여부 일괄 조회 메서드 추가

3. **`CommunityPostServiceImpl.java`**
   - `getPosts` 메서드를 2단계 쿼리 방식으로 변경
   - 댓글 수 및 좋아요 여부 일괄 조회로 변경

4. **`CommunityPost.java`**
   - `images` 컬렉션에 `@BatchSize(size = 100)` 추가

5. **`application.yml`**
   - `hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size: 100` 추가

6. **`CommunityPostServiceImplTest.java`**
   - 모든 `getPosts` 관련 테스트를 최적화된 코드에 맞게 수정

## 🧠 진행 이유

### 1. 페이징 정확성 문제 해결
- `LEFT JOIN FETCH p.images`를 사용할 때 row duplication으로 인해 페이징이 부정확하게 동작하는 문제를 해결했습니다.
- Post ID만 먼저 조회하여 페이징을 정확하게 처리하고, 이후 필요한 데이터를 조회하는 방식으로 변경했습니다.

### 2. N+1 문제 해결
- 댓글 수 조회와 좋아요 여부 조회에서 각 postId마다 개별 쿼리를 실행하던 문제를 해결했습니다.
- IN 절을 사용한 일괄 조회로 쿼리 수를 대폭 감소시켰습니다.

### 3. 성능 개선
- limit=10일 때:
  - **변경 전**: 1 (Post ID) + 1 (Post) + 10 (댓글 수) + 10 (좋아요) = **22개 쿼리**
  - **변경 후**: 1 (Post ID) + 1 (Post) + 1 (댓글 수) + 1 (좋아요) = **4개 쿼리**
- **약 82% 쿼리 수 감소**

### 4. Batch Fetching 활용
- images 컬렉션을 fetch join하지 않고도 `@BatchSize`로 인해 한 번의 쿼리로 모든 images를 로딩할 수 있도록 최적화했습니다.
- 페이징 문제를 해결하면서도 N+1 문제를 방지할 수 있습니다.

## ✅ 체크리스트
- [x] 단위 테스트 통과
- [x] 코드 컨벤션 준수
- [x] 성능 개선 검증
- [x] N+1 문제 해결
- [x] 페이징 정확성 개선
- [x] 테스트 코드 수정

## 📊 성능 개선 효과

### 쿼리 수 감소
- **변경 전**: 2N+1개 쿼리 (N = limit)
- **변경 후**: 4개 쿼리 (고정)
- **개선율**: 약 82% 감소 (limit=10 기준)

### 페이징 정확성
- **변경 전**: JOIN 결과 행 수 기준으로 페이징되어 부정확
- **변경 후**: Post ID 기준으로 정확한 페이징

### 확장성
- Post 수가 증가하거나 Image가 많은 Post가 있어도 쿼리 수가 일정하게 유지됩니다.
- 대용량 데이터에서도 안정적인 성능을 보장합니다.

Static website for a premium jewelry store, built with HTML + TailwindCSS (CDN) + vanilla JS. Fully compatible with GitHub Pages, no backend required.

## Pages
- **index.html** – Hero with parallax, category grid, featured products, benefits section, newsletter signup
- **catalogo.html** – 12 products with JS-based category filtering (Tradicional/Premium/Noivado/Personalizada)
- **sobre.html** – Company history, mission/values, team profiles, customer testimonials
- **contato.html** – Contact form, business info, map placeholder, FAQ accordion
- **produto.html** – Product detail template with image gallery, specs table, quote modal

## Features
- Sticky header with animated hamburger menu (mobile)
- Scroll-triggered fade-in animations via IntersectionObserver
- Quote request modal → `mailto:` integration
- Gold/cream/black premium color palette
- Playfair Display + Inter fonts via Google Fonts

/index.html
/catalogo.html
/sobre.html
/contato.html
/produto.html
/assets/          # 28 placeholder images (SVG)
/css/             # Reserved for custom styles

author: dakotamurphyucf
body:
## Summary
This PR teaches the chat TUI to understand and render tool outputs in a
tool-aware, syntax-highlighted way. Tool calls, file reads, directory
listings, and apply_patch responses now carry structured metadata through
the model and renderer so they can be displayed with appropriate styling.
## Changes
### Tool metadata and model plumbing
- Introduce `Types.tool_output_kind` to classify tool output messages in
  the TUI (e.g. `Read_file`, `Read_directory`, `Apply_patch`, etc.).
- Extend `Model.t` with a `tool_output_by_index` index and accessor to
  map message indices to `tool_output_kind` and any associated metadata
  (e.g. file path).
- Thread `tool_output_by_index` through:
  - `Model.create`
  - `App.run_chat` initialization
  - history replacement (`Replace_history`)
  - manual history compaction
- Track file paths for `read_file` / `read_directory` tool outputs in
  `tool_output_by_index` to support language inference and specialized
  rendering.
### Renderer: tool-aware rendering
- Extend `Paint.render_paragraph` to detect tool-call paragraphs for
  messages with `role = "tool"` and no `tool_output`, and:
  - Parse `name(args)` from the line.
  - Style the tool name with a dedicated attribute layered over the
    existing role colour.
  - Highlight the argument object as JSON using `Highlight_tm_engine`
    (`lang = Some "json"`), while preserving the exact message text and
    wrapping behaviour.
- For `Apply_patch` tool outputs (detected via `ctx.tool_output`):
  - Split the body into status text and patch body.
  - Render status lines as paragraphs.
  - Render the patch as a code block with `lang = "ochat-apply-patch"`,
    preserving the original text and headers.
- For `read_file` tool outputs:
  - Infer a language from the file extension (`.ml`, `.mli`, `.md`,
    `.json`, `.sh`, etc.) via `Renderer.lang_of_path`.
  - Render the output as a single syntax-highlighted code block when a
    language is known.
  - Fall back to the existing paragraph rendering when path or language
    is unknown.
- For `read_directory` tool outputs:
  - Use `tool_output_kind = Read_directory` to detect them.
  - Apply a uniform dim gray attribute to each directory entry line in
    `Paint.render_paragraph`.
  - Preserve original text, spacing, and wrapping so listings remain
    copy/paste friendly.
- Preserve markdown rendering for all non-tool messages and for tool
  messages that do not match the expected `name(args)` shape.
### Syntax highlighting, grammars, and theme
- Add a new TextMate grammar `ochat-apply-patch` in
  `Highlight_grammars`:
  - Match ochat’s V4A patch headers.
  - Delegate to the existing `source.diff` grammar for diff hunks.
  - Capture snippet line numbers and structured headers.
- Register the `ochat-apply-patch` grammar in `Highlight_registry` so
  it participates in the shared syntax-highlighting registry.
- Fix the JSON TextMate grammar so `json_tm_json` parses correctly and
  the `"json"` language now loads reliably.
- Extend `Highlight_theme` with rules for apply_patch snippets:
  - Green snippet text (`markup.inserted.ochatpatch`).
  - Red line-number prefixes
    (`constant.numeric.line-number.ochatpatch`).
  - Segmented headers: grey prefix, blue bold filename, and dim trailing
    ruler.
### Tests
- Add `chat_tui_tool_metadata_test`:
  - Expect tests for streaming `tool_output_kind` classification
    (`read_file`, `read_directory`, `apply_patch`).
  - History-based `rebuild_tool_output_index` tests for
    `read_file` / `read_directory` outputs, including path tracking.
  - Tests for `Renderer.lang_of_path` extension→language mapping
    (`.ml` / `.mli`, `.md`, `.json`, `.sh`, etc.).
- Add `chat_tui_tool_render_test`:
  - Exercises full `Renderer.render_full` output.
  - Verifies tool-call rendering preserves JSON call text.
  - Verifies `apply_patch` outputs keep status lines and patch headers.
  - Verifies `read_file` / `read_directory` outputs preserve file
    contents and directory entries while applying new styling.
  - Updates expectations for the new grammars and removes JSON grammar
    failure output.
- Wire the new test libraries into `test/dune`.
- Update existing chat-tui tests to construct models with the new
  `tool_output_by_index` field and to cover the new rendering paths.
## Rationale
These changes make tool interactions in the TUI significantly easier to
read and reason about:
- Tool calls show clearly separated names and JSON arguments.
- `read_file` results look like proper code blocks with language-aware
  syntax highlighting.
- `read_directory` results are visually distinct but still copy/paste
  friendly.
- `apply_patch` tool responses render as structured, coloured patches,
  aligned with how diffs are typically viewed.
All behaviour changes are covered by expect tests, making the new
rendering stable and regression-resistant.

Adds documentation describing the repository purpose and provides a standardized template for documenting LeetCode problem solutions.

## Changes

- **Repository description** - Overview of goals: high-performance solutions, code readability, optimal complexity
- **Problem template** - Reusable structure for each problem:
  - Problem metadata (number, name, difficulty, link)
  - Problem description and examples
  - Approach with time/space complexity analysis
  - Solution code block
  - Notes for edge cases

## Template Usage

```markdown
### Problem #1 - Two Sum

**Difficulty:** Easy

**LeetCode Link:** https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum

#### Problem Description
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target...

#### Approach
1. **Hash Map**
   - Time Complexity: O(n)
   - Space Complexity: O(n)

#### Solution
```python
def twoSum(nums, target):
    seen = {}
    for i, num in enumerate(nums):
        if target - num in seen:
            return [seen[target - num], i]
        seen[num] = i
```
```

author: towaiji
body:
Fixes #7333

This is a small bug fix.

This PR fixes an inconsistency in `recent_commits` where `limit == 0` still returns 1 commit due to the use of `limit.max(1)` when constructing the `git log -n` argument.

Expected behavior: requesting 0 commits should return an empty list.

This PR:
- returns an empty `Vec` when `limit == 0`
- adds a test for `recent_commits(limit == 0)` that fails before the change and passes afterwards
- maintains existing behavior for `limit > 0`

This aligns behavior with API expectations and avoids downstream consumers misinterpreting the repository as having commit history when `limit == 0` is used to explicitly request none.

Happy to adjust if the current behavior is intentional.

Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Angular is Vulnerable to XSRF Token Leakage via Protocol-Relative URLs in Angular HTTP Client

The vulnerability is a Credential Leak by App Logic that leads to the unauthorized disclosure of the Cross-Site Request Forgery (XSRF) token to an attacker-controlled domain.

Angular's HttpClient has a built-in XSRF protection mechanism that works by checking if a request URL starts with a protocol (http:// or https://) to determine if it is cross-origin. If the URL starts with protocol-relative URL (//), it is incorrectly treated as a same-origin request, and the XSRF token is automatically added to the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.

Impact

The token leakage completely bypasses Angular's built-in CSRF protection, allowing an attacker to capture the user's valid XSRF token. Once the token is obtained, the attacker can perform arbitrary Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks against the victim user's session.

Attack Preconditions

  1. The victim's Angular application must have XSRF protection enabled.
  2. The attacker must be able to make the application send a state-changing HTTP request (e.g., POST) to a protocol-relative URL (e.g., //attacker.com) that they control.

Patches

  • 19.2.16
  • 20.3.14
  • 21.0.1

Workarounds

Developers should avoid using protocol-relative URLs (URLs starting with //) in HttpClient requests. All backend communication URLs should be hardcoded as relative paths (starting with a single /) or fully qualified, trusted absolute URLs.

The token leakage completely bypasses Angular's built-in CSRF protection, allowing an attacker to capture the user's valid XSRF token. Once the token is obtained, the attacker can perform arbitrary Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks against the victim user's session.

# Pull Request: Fix Truncated Tool Results Not Showing in Chat Client

## Summary
Truncated system log messages from the orchestration layer were not displaying in the chat-client. When tool results exceed token limits, the PHP orchestration layer truncates them to strings with a marker—these strings were being silently discarded.

## Issue
**Problem**: `normaliseToolResultForDisplay()` only handled object results, returning `null` for strings. Truncated tool results (converted to strings by orchestration layer) never appeared in chat.

**Solution**: Handle string results in `normaliseToolResultForDisplay()` before the object-only check.

## Changes Made

### Code Changes (2 files)

#### 1. String Result Handling
- ✅ `assets/js/chat.js` - Added string handling at start of `normaliseToolResultForDisplay()`

```javascript
// Handle string results (e.g., truncated tool results from orchestration layer)
if (typeof result === 'string' && result.trim()) {
    return {
        text: result,
        attachments: []
    };
}
```

body:
## Summary
- Fixed SAWarning that occurred when using sqlacodegen with SQLAlchemy 2.0
- Changed `metadata.reflect()` call to use explicit keyword arguments instead of positional arguments

## Problem
When running sqlacodegen with SQLAlchemy 2.0, the following warning was displayed:

```
SAWarning: Can't validate argument 'dialect_options'; can't locate any SQLAlchemy dialect named 'dialect'
```

This occurred because positional arguments were being passed to `MetaData.reflect()`, which in SQLAlchemy 2.0 expects keyword arguments after the first positional argument (bind).

## Changes
Changed line 59 in `src/sqlacodegen/cli.py`:

**Before:**
```python
metadata.reflect(engine, schema, not args.noviews, tables)
```

author: junghoon-vans
body:
## Summary

Add gas measurement report generation feature to the bless tool. This allows generating markdown and TSV reports from txtar integration tests for gas analysis.

## Changes

- Add `-report` flag for markdown report generation
- Add `-tsv` flag for TSV output with auto-generated timestamped filename
- Parse function names from `-func` parameter in gnokey commands
- Support category grouping via `### Category ###` headers in txtar
- Calculate pure gas usage (total - baseline) using `Empty` function as baseline
- Add Makefile commands for easy usage

## Usage

```bash
# Install txtar-bless tool
make bless-install

# Generate markdown report (stdout)
make gas-report TEST=uint256_gas_measurement

# Generate TSV file (auto-generates filename with timestamp)
make gas-report-tsv TEST=uint256_gas_measurement
# → uint256_gas_measurement_20251127_124049.tsv
```

## Output Format

### Markdown
```markdown
# Gas Measurement Report: uint256_gas_measurement

**Baseline (Empty Call):** 451,086 gas

## Constructor Methods

| Name | Pure Gas Used | Total Gas Used | Method Call Cost | Storage (bytes) |
|------|---------------|----------------|------------------|----------------|
| TestNewUint | 2,246,981 | 2,698,067 | 451,086 | 0 |
```

### TSV
```
Name	Category	Pure Gas Used	Total Gas Used	Method Call Cost	Storage (bytes)
TestNewUint	Constructor Methods	2246981	2698067	451086	0
```

## Writing Gas Measurement Tests

To create a gas measurement txtar test:

### 1. Create txtar file

Create file in `tests/integration/testdata/<test_name>.txtar`

### 2. Define Empty baseline function

The `Empty` function is used to calculate the baseline (method call overhead):

```
gnokey maketx call -pkgpath gno.land/r/test -func Empty ...
```

### 3. Use category headers

Group related functions with headers:

```
### Constructor Methods ###
### Arithmetic Operations ###
```

### 4. Call test functions

```
gnokey maketx call -pkgpath gno.land/r/test -func TestNewUint ...
gnokey maketx call -pkgpath gno.land/r/test -func TestAdd ...
```

### 5. Create symlink

```bash
ln -sf $(pwd)/tests/integration/testdata/test.txtar \
       ~/gno/gno.land/pkg/integration/testdata/test.txtar
```

### 6. Generate report

```bash
make gas-report TEST=test
make gas-report-tsv TEST=test
```

author: gday
body:
Previously, ChiefOnboarding only allowed one start date. Everything was based on the `user.start_day`. This changes with this PR. 

A user could be added to multiple roles and for each role, they might start on a different day. The sequences that are in that role should accommodate to that. 

The change being made here adds a `base_date` to the `conditions` and time based items (`to do` and `resources`). Introductions and badges etc are not affected as they don't have timing. 

Instead of comparing against the `start_day` we now compare against the `base_date` that is being set in those M2M `through` models. The `base_date` is being set based on the new date field when someone gets dragged into the role.

For new hires, we sometimes still check against `start_day`. This is fine, new hires have been excluded from the departments list page. They can only be added to a role once they are converted to a normal user. This means that a new hire can only have one start day.

For extra clearance:
`workday()` skips all weekends and gets the actual workday of the user. So, when they start on monday, it's day 1 and next week monday is day 6.
`days_before_starting()` is slightly different as weekends are counted, these are the actual days before the user starts.
`days_before_termination_date()` is not affected as a user will be offboarded in full, so there is only one date for this.

Também reorganiza os arquivos de configuração do Django, adiciona Celery para tarefas assíncronas, configura Nginx como proxy reverso e atualiza a documentação dos principais módulos.

## Principais Mudanças

- Três arquivos Docker Compose:

- docker-compose.yml – ambiente completo

- docker-compose.local.yml – ambiente híbrido (Django no host; serviços em containers)

- Health checks configurados

- Script de inicialização unificado (entrypoint.sh)

- PostgreSQL

- Redis

- Django (Gunicorn)

- Celery Worker

- Celery Beat

- Nginx

### Settings Modularizados

Reorganização completa dos settings para suportar diferentes ambientes:

wedding_management/settings/
├── __init__.py
├── base.py
├── local.py
├── production.py
└── test.py


O antigo settings.py único foi removido.

### Celery

- Configuração central adicionada

- Execução via worker e beat

- Tasks organizadas em apps/core/tasks.py

### Documentação

- DOCKER.md: guia completo para uso do Docker

- READMEs atualizados nos principais apps

- .env.example revisado com variáveis essenciais

### Requirements

Separação em:

- base.txt

- local.txt

- production.txt

- test.txt

## Estatísticas Gerais

- 39 arquivos alterados

- Aproximadamente +4.195 linhas líquidas

## Observações

O PR é extenso, mas estabelece a base necessária para suporte completo ao Docker e separação clara de ambientes. Ajustes futuros podem incluir integração com CI/CD e ferramentas de monitoramento.

author: pietbarber
body:
## Summary
Fixes #298 - The towplane logbook page was extremely slow for towplanes with 10+ years of operational history, with load times exceeding 10,000 milliseconds.

## Problem
The original `towplane_logbook` view had severe N+1 query issues:

1. **Per-day flight queries**: For each closeout day, ran a separate `Flight.objects.filter()` query
2. **Per-day issue queries**: Called `_issues_by_day_for_towplane()` inside the loop, re-running the same query N times
3. **Member lookups not batched**: Tow pilot names resolved inefficiently

For a towplane with 1,000 operating days, this resulted in **2,000+ queries** and 10+ second load times.

## Solution
Applied the same batch-loading pattern used in #297 (instruction record performance):

1. **Pre-fetch ALL flights in one query** - Single query with `values()`, bucket by day in Python
2. **Pre-fetch ALL member names in one query** - Using `.filter(id__in=...)` with `.only()` for efficiency
3. **Pre-fetch ALL maintenance issues once** - Call `_issues_by_day_for_towplane()` before the loop, not inside it
4. **Use dict lookups** - O(1) lookups replace O(n) queries

## Results

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Queries (100 days) | 200+ | ~10 |
| Queries (1000 days) | 2000+ | ~10 |
| Load time (10+ years) | >10 seconds | <1 second |
| Query complexity | O(days) | O(1) |

## Testing
- All 152 existing logsheet tests pass
- Added 5 new performance tests in `test_towplane_logbook_performance.py`:
  - `test_towplane_logbook_query_count`: Verifies query count stays under 20
  - `test_towplane_logbook_data_integrity`: Verifies data correctness with batch loading
  - `test_query_analysis`: Validates specific query patterns are batched
  - `test_empty_logbook`: Edge case with no data
  - `test_single_day_logbook`: Edge case with minimal data

## Files Changed
- `logsheet/views.py`: Rewrote `towplane_logbook()` view with batch queries
- `logsheet/tests/test_towplane_logbook_performance.py`: New performance tests
- `docs/resolved-issues/issue-298-towplane-logbook-performance.md`: Documentation

author: bitshifter-9
body:
The uv__fs_to_timespec function in src/unix/fs.c currently truncates nanoseconds to microseconds. This was originally implemented for consistency with other platforms, but as noted in a TODO comment, utimesat() supports nanosecond resolution.

This commit removes the truncation to allow full nanosecond precision where supported by the underlying filesystem. It also improves the double-to-timespec conversion to use rounding, fixing precision issues.

- Removed the line `ts.tv_nsec -= ts.tv_nsec % 1000;` in `src/unix/fs.c`.
- Improved `double` to `timespec` conversion to use rounding instead of truncation to fix floating-point precision issues.
- Added a verification test case in `test/test-fs.c`.

author: integerman
body:
This pull request introduces a new document embedding worker to the project, improves the handling of Qdrant point IDs to avoid collisions, and adds support for embedding-related configuration and message consumption. The changes enhance the reliability of embedding storage and retrieval, and integrate the new worker with existing infrastructure.

**Document Embedding Worker Integration:**

* Added a new project, `JAIMES AF.Workers.DocumentEmbedding`, to the solution and registered it in the app host, including environment variable setup for Ollama and Qdrant endpoints and API keys. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d63f57cc75cf6cbdf6381a1bda156cbf2bc036c021af155654351682916ea675R1-R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0a2e32be174bf2be4f042ff1f5b31d511815778dc2c745dab7d8b326ecc64ba2R19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-765b8215352da8635d7f5a603516786e31929eb21008397a72ec5b44a4d1fe35R169-R194)
* Registered the document embedding worker in `AppHost.cs`, with dependencies on LavinMQ, MongoDB, Qdrant, and the embedding model, and configured environment variables for service connectivity.

**Qdrant Point ID Handling Improvements:**

* Replaced the use of `GetHashCode()` with a SHA256-based hashing method to generate Qdrant point IDs, preventing collisions and ensuring consistent point ID mapping across embedding operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb50be196c25035a95697297ab5a313d1121b1e9ab274d4ca064ad8c557856fcR18-R32) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cb50be196c25035a95697297ab5a313d1121b1e9ab274d4ca064ad8c557856fcL114-R133) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cb50be196c25035a95697297ab5a313d1121b1e9ab274d4ca064ad8c557856fcL197-R211) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cb50be196c25035a95697297ab5a313d1121b1e9ab274d4ca064ad8c557856fcL243-R256) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-cb50be196c25035a95697297ab5a313d1121b1e9ab274d4ca064ad8c557856fcL321-R336)

**Embedding Message Consumption and Configuration:**

* Added a consumer, `ChunkReadyForEmbeddingConsumer`, that validates and processes chunk embedding messages using the new embedding service.
* Introduced configuration classes for embedding options and Qdrant connection string parsing, supporting flexible setup of embedding dimensions, collection names, and connection parameters. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d1c4986bde4e3bb23080a9e216ec3ba099f47f3efd08233c9c55a73e2e5c7e39R1-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4ea8d51c05aebb82f772a43254c60f00647400c41d74534d4d9e2b7a1d0a24eR1-R136)

**Data Model Update:**

* Updated the `DocumentChunk` model to include an optional `QdrantPointId` field for tracking the corresponding embedding in Qdrant.

**Miscellaneous:**

* Removed an unused test runner property and cleaned up parameters related to document change detection in the app host. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3ffa7096e43739b40bf9cac3dd1a6cfde23fbde21caec1040e828c3bc189f688L12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-765b8215352da8635d7f5a603516786e31929eb21008397a72ec5b44a4d1fe35L60-L63) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-765b8215352da8635d7f5a603516786e31929eb21008397a72ec5b44a4d1fe35L148-R144)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds a new document-embedding worker, centralizes Qdrant client configuration, and switches to collision-safe SHA256 point IDs with model support to track them.
> 
> - **Workers**:
>   - **Document Embedding**: New project `JAIMES AF.Workers.DocumentEmbedding` (program, service, consumer, options, appsettings) to generate embeddings via Ollama and store them in Qdrant.
>   - Registered in `AppHost.cs` with LavinMQ/Mongo/Qdrant/Ollama references and env vars.
> - **Qdrant Integration**:
>   - **Centralized config**: New `QdrantExtensions.AddQdrantClient` and `QdrantConnectionStringParser` in `ServiceDefaults`; `Qdrant.Client` added to shared project.
>   - ApiService and DocumentChunking now use `AddQdrantClient`; removed bespoke connection parsing/helpers from `ApiService/Program.cs`.
> - **Embedding IDs**:
>   - Replace `GetHashCode()` with SHA256-based `ulong` IDs in `QdrantEmbeddingStore` (store/list/delete) and matching logic in embedding worker.
>   - Data model: `DocumentChunk` gains optional `qdrantPointId`.
> - **AppHost/Solution**:
>   - AppHost wires endpoints/API key for Qdrant to chunking/embedding workers; adds project reference for embedding worker; solution updated.
> - **Misc**:
>   - Minor cleanup in AppHost (removed unused parameter) and tests project property.

body: ## What’s in this PR: ### 1. Schedule ↔ ToDo Synchronization: - Introduced full two-way sync between the Schedule screen and the ToDo system. - Todos from ToDoRepository now appear inside: - Day view → only todos due on the selected date. - Week view → only todos whose due date falls in the selected week. - Adding a ToDo from ScheduleScreen now saves it in ToDoRepository, meaning: - It appears immediately in ToDo list. - It also appears back in Schedule (Day/Week sections) after navigation. ### 2. Navigation: **Schedule → Add ToDo → Back to Schedule:** - Added a custom navigation route: addTodoFromSchedule/{date} - FloatingActionButton on Schedule now opens ToDo creation without switching to the ToDo screen. - After saving a ToDo, the user is returned directly back to the same view inside Schedule (Day or Week). **Schedule's todo → Todos screen:** - Acces to todo screen through the todos in schedule. ### 4. UI Components Updated: - DayTabContent: Added a new Todos section box using the same visual structure as Classes & Objectives. - WeekTabContent: Added filtering of todos by week. - Adjusted FAB behavior so it only appears in Day/Week tabs. ## Implementation Notes: ### Key Decisions & Trade-offs: Kept ToDo and Schedule logic decoupled via repositories instead of merging entities. Decided not to directly convert ToDo into ScheduleEvent to avoid breaking Schedule logic. Navigation uses a dedicated temporary route to avoid modifying ToDo module internals. ## Testing: - Unit Tests for ViewModel added methods Navigation callback logic tested via mocks. - UI / Instrumented Tests: FloatingActionButton appears only in DAY/WEEK. Adding a ToDo from Schedule returns back to Schedule. DayTabContent correctly displays todos for selected date. WeekTabContent correctly displays todos for selected week. No regressions in existing ToDo tests. ## Screenshots: ## Checklist: - [x] Todos visible in Day View - [x] Todos visible in Week View - [x] Add ToDo from Schedule works - [x] Navigation returns properly - [x] All unit + UI tests pass ## Notes: This pr was implemented with the help of ia (chatgpt). ## Issue Reference: Closes #187

author: nathanvale
body:
## Summary

Complete migration from Node.js/pnpm toolchain to Bun runtime and ecosystem. This PR modernizes the development stack while maintaining all functionality and test coverage.

## Type

- [x] refactor
- [ ] feat
- [ ] fix
- [ ] docs
- [ ] test
- [ ] ci/build/chore

## Changes

### Build & Runtime
- **Bun runtime** - Replace Node.js with Bun for runtime and package management
- **Biome** - Replace ESLint + Prettier with Biome for unified linting/formatting
- **Bun test runner** - Replace Vitest with Bun's native test runner
- **Remove pnpm** - Delete pnpm-lock.yaml, .npmrc, migrate to bun.lock

### Code Organization
- **Extract link enrichment providers** - Modularize providers (YouTube, Spotify, Twitter, Instagram, Firecrawl, Generic) into `src/enrich/providers/`
- **Modularize CLI** - Split monolithic CLI into separate command modules in `src/cli/commands/`
- **Improve output handling** - Migrate from `console.info` to `humanInfo` utility for better logging control

### Configuration
- **bunup.config.ts** - Add Bun update configuration
- **biome.json** - New unified formatter/linter config
- **Remove legacy configs** - Delete eslint.config.js, prettier.config.mjs, vitest.config.ts
- **Update Renovate** - Configure for Bun package manager

### Testing
- All tests migrated to Bun test format
- Snapshot tests updated for deterministic output
- Coverage metrics script updated for Bun
- Pre-commit hooks updated for Biome

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits (e.g., feat(scope): summary)
- [x] Lint/Typecheck/Test pass
- [x] Included docs/notes when behavior changes

## Test Results

```bash
# All tests passing with Bun
bun test

# Biome formatting and linting
bun biome check .
```

## Migration Impact

**Breaking Changes:**
- None - this is an internal tooling change

**Developer Experience:**
- Faster test execution with Bun
- Unified linting/formatting reduces cognitive load
- Simpler dependency management (single lockfile)
- Better TypeScript performance

**Files Changed:**
- 155 files changed, +36,502 -41,171 (net reduction of ~4,669 lines)
- Removed 22 legacy Claude config files
- Added modular structure for CLI and providers

## Notes

This migration maintains 100% backward compatibility with the existing API and data formats. All tests pass. The primary motivation is improved DX (developer experience) through:

1. **Speed** - Bun's faster runtime and test execution
2. **Simplicity** - Single tool (Biome) vs ESLint+Prettier
3. **Modern toolchain** - Leveraging Bun's native features

The modularization of CLI and providers improves maintainability and follows single-responsibility principles.

---

author: duncaneddy
body:
# Pull Request

## Description

This PR Implements Numerical Propagation for both satellite orbits as well as generic numerical propagators.

In implementing these changes there were a few design decision that became apparent. First is that python bindings should standardize on implementing either S-type or D-type propagators given python's interpreted nature, I decided to standardize on having all python bindings implement the D-type propagator and dropped the `D` to improving naming.

## Changelog

### Added
- `{D}NumericalOrbitPropagator` and python bindings
- `{D}NumericalPropagator` and python bindings
- Event detection system for numerical propagators to find events during propagation

### Changed
- Make access computation use D-type propagators.
- Standardize on 
- Add support for D-type returns to `KeplerianPropagator` and `SGPPropagator` 
- Standardized trait traits for `{S|D}StateProvider`, `{S|D}CovarianceProvider`, `{S|D}StatePropagator`
- `DTrajectory` and `DOrbitTrajectory` can now store trajectories of arbitrary length
- `DTrajectory` and `DOrbitTrajectory` can now store stm and sensitivity matricies alongside state and covariance.
- Improved test coverage across modules
- Changed how third-body ephemeris sources are defined and loaded. DE source is now a parameter instead of set by function name. Dynamically load BSP files when called.
- Changed how Gravity models are defined in terms of enumeration types.
- Renamed `state_cartesian_to_osculating` and `state_osculating_to_cartesian` as `state_eci_to_koe` and `state_koe_to_eci`

### Fixed
- Numerical integration `step` and `step_with_varmat` now take explicit parameter values.

### Removed
- Removed `STrajectory6` from python bindings.

author: disinvite
body:
- New entity types: `THUNK` and `VTORDISP`. `THUNK` will be used for incremental build (debug) thunks. Import thunks will keep using the `FUNCTION` type. The distinction is that `THUNK` entities acquire the `Thunk of` prefix.

- Created a new `refs` SQL table for storing links between entities. We no longer need `ref_orig` and `ref_recomp` attributes on the main `entities` table. `refs` has a column for the `ImageId` enum to specify which address space we are in.

- The new `set_ref` function on the DB batch creates the link between entities. Ref information now includes the two displacement values so we can match vtordisp functions along with thunks. Thunks have a displacement value of `(0, 0)`.

- The new approach for naming thunks and vtordisps is: start by copying each function name into a new `names` SQL table. Using the data from `refs`, copy the parent's names to each child function. We can run this repeatedly to cover chains of thunks. `BETA10` has many instances of: thunk -> vtordisp -> thunk -> function.

- The database function `get_functions()` returns all matched `FUNCTION`, `THUNK`, or `VTORDISP` entities. The ghidra script will need some changes to handle thunks differently so I thought it best to just keep the same behavior for now.

- In chat we discussed omitting vtordisps from the diff report. I decided not to do it here but it's a one line change when we're ready.

My end goal for this is to have a series of "stage" tables where we collect data points (names, sizes, types) from all available sources, decide which are the most likely to describe the entity (e.g. prefer user data over autodetect), then match and build the final list of entities.

To achieve that, I need to change the behavior of `get_by_orig` and `get_by_recomp`, and not using them while matching thunks is the first step.

This allows removing version shorteners for Twingate and Citrix Workspace that were only shortening dot-separated version strings. This also allows for our FMA library on fleetdm.com to represent more accurate version strings.

- Add HasPrefix check for expected version starting with found version
- Remove TwingateVersionShortener
- Remove CitrixWorkspaceVersionShortener
- Remove citrix_workspace_version_shortener_test.go

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
Refactored the monolithic `SQLiteManager` class into a DAO (Data Access Object) pattern to improve code structure, maintainability, and scalability.

Changes:
1.  **Created `ConexionDB`**: Encapsulates the JDBC connection logic (Singleton).
2.  **Created DAOs**:
    *   `UsuarioDAO`: Handles user authentication and management.
    *   `ProductoDAO`: Handles product inventory operations.
    *   `ComprobanteCompraDAO`: Handles purchase receipts.
    *   `ComprobanteVentaDAO`: Handles sales receipts.
    *   `AjustesDAO`: Handles application settings.
3.  **Refactored `SQLiteManager`**: Now acts as a **Facade**, delegating all operations to the respective DAOs. This preserves the existing API so no changes were needed in the UI layer.
4.  **Optimized Resource Management**: All database operations now use `try-with-resources` to ensure connections and statements are closed properly.
5.  **Language**: Kept all code and comments in Spanish.

---

body: Implement a ship traffic flow visualization and analysis system to load AIS data, display trajectories, perform spatial analysis, and generate heatmaps. ---   --- > [!NOTE] > Introduce a pure-frontend Leaflet app to load AIS CSV, visualize trajectories/heatmaps, and perform area/cross-section traffic analyses with stats. > > - **Frontend/UI**: > - Add `index.html` with sidebar controls (data load, MMSI filter, analysis tools, visualization toggles) and map container. > - Add `styles.css` for layout, controls, and stats styling. > - **Core Functionality (`app.js`)**: > - Initialize Leaflet map with OSM tiles and drawing tools (`leaflet-draw`). > - Load and parse AIS CSV via `PapaParse`; compute dataset stats and time range. > - Visualize ship trajectories with speed-based coloring and start/end markers; toggle show/hide. > - Filter displayed data by MMSI and update counts. > - Generate heatmap layer (`Leaflet.heat`) with configurable gradient; toggle show/hide. > - Spatial analyses: > - Area analysis (polygon/rectangle): compute traffic flow (ships/hour), average speed, density (ships/km²), and ship count. > - Cross-section analysis (polyline): compute nearby traffic, average speed, density (ships/km), and ship count. > - Utilities for area/line calculations, point-to-line distance, and view reset. > - **Data**: > - Add `sample_ais_data.csv` for demo/testing. > - **Docs**: > - Replace `README.md` with Chinese documentation covering features, data format, usage, tech stack, and project structure. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 5ff5843b5bb5face31e2dcd37c882188e37e777d. author: tgxworld
body:
Prior to this change, the SQL query string returned by `BadgeQueries.sharing_badge`
was simply counting the number of `incoming_links` rows for a given post
and sharer (user_id). This is however incorrect as the sharing badges
description states that the visitors have to be unique.

This commit updates `BadgeQueries.sharing_badge` to count only unique (ip_address, current_user_id) pairs in incoming_links, so repeated hits from the same visitor no longer inflate share badge counts.

author: savid
body:
External models with (0, 0) bounds were not being skipped in OR group processing, causing the union to incorrectly use min=0. This made backfill scan from position 0 forever even when no OR dependencies had data that far back.

The fix extends the existing transformation check to skip any dependency (external or transformation) with (0, 0) bounds.

<!-- DO NOT IGNORE THE TEMPLATE!

Thank you for contributing!

Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following:

- Read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/shikijs/shiki/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- Check that there isn't already a PR that solves the problem the same way to avoid creating a duplicate.
- Provide a description in this PR that addresses **what** the PR is solving, or reference the issue that it solves (e.g. `fixes #123`).
- Ideally, include relevant tests that fail without this PR but pass with it.

-->

### Description

This PR adds support for the embeddedLanguages field in LanguageRegistration.

Historically the field was named embeddedLangs, while VSCode grammars use embeddedLanguages.
Shiki currently supports only embeddedLangs, which prevents grammars using the VSCode naming convention from working as expected.

### Linked Issues
Fixes #1044

### Additional context

No breaking changes introduced — if both fields are present, embeddedLanguages takes priority.
This brings Shiki in line with VSCode terminology while preserving support for older grammars.

<textarea
  id="ticket-reply-body-hidden"
  name="body"
  class="visually-hidden"
  aria-hidden="true"
  data-rich-text-value   <!-- was missing -->
  required
>{{ reply_body }}</textarea>
```

Consistent with existing implementations in `admin/ticket_detail.html` and `tickets/index.html`.

author: williamberryiii
body:
## Description

This PR applies comprehensive editorial improvements to the preface following the markdown style guide standards defined in `markdown-styleguide.instructions.md`. The changes transform the preface from formal academic prose into conversational, scannable content that aligns with Nielsen Norman Group research on web reading patterns.

## Related Issue(s)

Closes #17

## Editorial Improvements Applied

### 1. Sentence Length Reduction
* Reduced average sentence length to 15-20 words for better comprehension
* Split complex 36-word and 25-word sentences into shorter, digestible statements
* Improved information flow and reader cognitive load

### 2. Bold Formatting on Key Terms
* **RPI framework** (first mention)
* **Task Researcher**, **Task Planner**, **Task Implementer** chat modes
* **discoverability principle**
* **meta-cognitive shift** concept

### 3. Paragraph Restructuring
* Restructured to 3-4 sentences per paragraph following inverted pyramid pattern
* Applied sentence case to subheadings (not title case)
* Enhanced scanability with H3 subheadings for navigation

### 4. Voice and Tone Improvements
* Converted passive voice to active voice throughout
* Added contractions for conversational tone ("you'll" vs "you will")
* Applied parallel structure to closing paragraph for rhythm and impact

### 5. Enhanced Navigation
* Added 5 H3 subheadings:
  * The Framework You'll Master
  * The Chat Modes You'll Use
  * The Principle That Changes Everything
  * The Shift You'll Experience
  * What You'll Take Away
* Improved document structure and scanability

### 6. Scannable Content
* Added 4 bullet lists for key concepts:
  * Chat mode capabilities (Task Researcher, Task Planner, Task Implementer)
  * HVE Core benefits (shared knowledge, prompt engineering, workflow patterns)
  * Mindset shifts (code exploration, systematic thinking, trust + verification)
  * Reader outcomes (confidence, speed, quality)

### 7. Document Footer
* Added attribution footer with team acknowledgment

## Testing

* ✅ Verified markdown syntax compliance with markdownlint
* ✅ Confirmed frontmatter validation passes
* ✅ Checked reading level targets (Flesch-Kincaid 10-12th grade)
* ✅ Validated accessibility requirements (semantic headings, scannable structure)

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)

## Checklist

- [x] My changes follow the naming conventions of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own changes
- [x] I have commented my code/docs, particularly in hard-to-understand areas (if applicable)
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works (if applicable)
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (if applicable)
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules (if applicable)

## Additional Notes

This editorial work demonstrates the application of evidence-based writing standards (Nielsen Norman Group research, Microsoft/Google/GitHub style guides) to improve reader comprehension and engagement. The preface now models the conversational, scannable style that the guide teaches throughout.

author: copilot
body:
CI failing due to pylint E1101 "no-member" error when accessing `_decorator_metadata` set by `@plugin` decorator.

## Problem

The `@plugin` decorator sets `_decorator_metadata` as a **class** attribute, but `_create_metadata()` was accessing it as an **instance** attribute:

```python
def _create_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
    return self._decorator_metadata  # E1101: no '_decorator_metadata' member
```

## Fix

- Access via class attribute: `self.__class__._decorator_metadata`
- Add defensive `hasattr()` check with fallback metadata
- Follows pattern used by builtin plugins in `src/transformation_portal/plugins/builtin/depth_models.py`

```python
def _create_metadata(self) -> PluginMetadata:
    if hasattr(self.__class__, '_decorator_metadata'):
        return self.__class__._decorator_metadata
    
    # Fallback if decorator wasn't used
    return PluginMetadata(...)
```

body:
Implements robust error handling with loop detection, timeouts, crash recovery, and graceful degradation to prevent infinite loops, handle hanging operations, recover from crashes, and continue with reduced functionality when components fail.

## New Modules

- **`loop_detector.py`** - Tracks task attempts, enforces max retries (default 3), escalates to ErrorHandler after limit
- **`timeout_manager.py`** - Configurable timeouts: API (60s), task (5min), stage (30min), project (2h)
- **`crash_recovery.py`** - SQLite checkpoints after each stage, restores incomplete projects on startup
- **`error_recovery.py`** - Classifies errors (transient, rate_limit, auth, validation, timeout, resource, logic), determines action (retry, skip, escalate, abort)
- **`graceful_degradation.py`** - Backup agents/providers, degradation levels, continues with warnings for non-critical failures

## Orchestrator Integration

- Checkpoints saved after stage transitions
- Tasks run with timeout wrapper
- Failed tasks use error recovery with retry/backoff
- Missing agents trigger graceful degradation
- New methods: `recover_project()`, `get_error_handling_stats()`

## Usage

```python
orchestrator = Orchestrator()
await orchestrator.initialize()  # Checks for incomplete projects

# Error handling is automatic during task execution
result = await orchestrator.start_development(project_id, plan)

# Recover from crash
recovered = await orchestrator.recover_project("proj-123")

# Get diagnostics
stats = orchestrator.get_error_handling_stats()
```

## Tests

53 new tests covering all components and integration scenarios.

```

```python
class ErrorRecovery:

        - message: explanation
        """

    async def try_alternative_approach(self, task: dict, error: dict) -> dict:
        """Get alternative approach from ErrorHandlerAgent."""
        pass
```

### Part 5: Graceful Degradation (`backend/core/graceful_degradation.py`)

Handle partial failures gracefully:

```python
class GracefulDegradation:
    def __init__(self):
        pass
    
    async def on_agent_failure(self, agent_name: str, error: Exception) -> str:
        """
        Handle agent failure:

Update `backend/core/orchestrator.py`:
- Use LoopDetector for task retries

<summary>digitalbazaar/forge (node-forge)</summary>

### [`v1.3.2`](https://redirect.github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#132---2025-11-25)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2)

##### Security

- **HIGH**: ASN.1 Validator Desynchronization
  - An Interpretation Conflict (CWE-436) vulnerability in node-forge versions
    1.3.1 and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to craft ASN.1
    structures to desynchronize schema validations, yielding a semantic
    divergence that may bypass downstream cryptographic verifications and
    security decisions.
  - Reported by Hunter Wodzenski.
  - CVE ID: [CVE-2025-12816](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-12816)
  - GHSA ID: [GHSA-5gfm-wpxj-wjgq](https://redirect.github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/security/advisories/GHSA-5gfm-wpxj-wjgq)
- **HIGH**: ASN.1 Unbounded Recursion
  - An Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674) vulnerability in node-forge versions
    1.3.1 and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to craft deep
    ASN.1 structures that trigger unbounded recursive parsing. This leads to a
    Denial-of-Service (DoS) via stack exhaustion when parsing untrusted DER
    inputs.
  - Reported by Hunter Wodzenski.
  - CVE ID: [CVE-2025-66031](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-66031)
  - GHSA ID: [GHSA-554w-wpv2-vw27](https://redirect.github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/security/advisories/GHSA-554w-wpv2-vw27)
- **MODERATE**: ASN.1 OID Integer Truncation
  - An Integer Overflow (CWE-190) vulnerability in node-forge versions 1.3.1
    and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to craft ASN.1
    structures containing OIDs with oversized arcs. These arcs may be decoded
    as smaller, trusted OIDs due to 32-bit bitwise truncation, enabling the
    bypass of downstream OID-based security decisions.
  - Reported by Hunter Wodzenski.
  - CVE ID: [CVE-2025-66030](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-66030)
  - GHSA ID: [GHSA-65ch-62r8-g69g](https://redirect.github.com/digitalbazaar/forge/security/advisories/GHSA-65ch-62r8-g69g)

##### Fixed

- \[asn1] Fix for vulnerability identified by CVE-2025-12816 [PKCS#12](https://redirect.github.com/PKCS/forge/issues/12) MAC
  verification bypass due to missing macData enforcement and improper
  asn1.validate routine.
- \[asn1] Add `fromDer()` max recursion depth check.
  - Add a `asn1.maxDepth` global configurable maximum depth of 256.
  - Add a `asn1.fromDer()` per-call `maxDepth` option.
  - **NOTE**: The default maximum is assumed to be higher than needed for valid
    data. If this assumption is false then this could be a breaking change.
    Please file an issue if there are use cases that need a higher maximum.
  - **NOTE**: The per-call `maxDepth` parameter has not been exposed up through
    all of the API stack due to the complexities involved. Please file an issue
    if there are use cases that require this instead of changing the default
    maximum.
- \[asn1] Improve OID handling.
  - Error on parsed OID values larger than `2**32 - 1`.
  - Error on DER OID values larger than `2**53 - 1 `.

</details>

author: cblecker
body:
## Summary
This PR adds automatic platform labeling to the OWNERS file for all 8 supported platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, IBMCloud, KubeVirt, None, OpenStack, PowerVS). PRs and issues will now be automatically labeled with `area/platform/*` labels based on the files they touch.

## Changes
- Consolidates existing GCP, KubeVirt, and OpenStack reviewer patterns from multiple patterns into single optimized patterns per platform
- Adds `area/platform/*` labels to existing platform patterns (GCP, KubeVirt, OpenStack)
- Adds new platform-specific label patterns for AWS, Azure, IBMCloud, None, and PowerVS
- Reorganizes all platform patterns into a single consolidated section for easier maintenance

## Pattern Format
Each platform uses a single regex pattern matching the platform name in these directories:
- `api`, `cmd`, `control-plane-operator`, `docs`, `hypershift-operator`, `product-cli`, `test`
- Exception: `none` platform has a more limited scope

## Impact
- **Before**: ~35 separate patterns scattered across the file
- **After**: 8 consolidated patterns in one organized section
- All 8 platforms now have automatic labeling when platform-specific code is touched

author: rekgrpth
body:
Fix inconsistency DROP IF EXISTS command

When the DROP IF EXISTS command is called, it is unconditionally dispatched to
the segments, even if the object doesn't exist on the coordinator. This can
lead to inconsistencies, for example:

- the first session starts a table drop on the coordinator. Even though the
table doesn't exist, the drop is still dispatched to the segments.

- at the same time, the second session creates the table (on the coordinator
and on the segments).

- the first session (on the segments) already sees the table and therefore
deletes it.

Don't dispatch DROP if object doesn't exist on coordinator. Exclude the
drop_rename test from the parallel group because it contains fault-injectors.
Add a new GUC, gp_dispatch_drop_always, for unconditional DROP dispatch even if
the object isn't present on the coordinator, as this functionality is used by
the gpcheckcat utility, for example, in the orphan_temp_table test.

(cherry picked from commit 3bd88175e9906db0bef54b64ac944cc5eda0f32c)

Changes:

1) The RemoveObjects function no longer has the local variable cell2 and the
condition with stmt->arguments to fill it.

2) The ExecDropStmt function no longer has the OBJECT_EXTTABLE case.

3) The condition on stmt->removeType in the ExecDropStmt function has been
generalized using the shouldDispatchForObject function.

4) The output has been adapted in the drop_rename and direct_dispatch tests.

5) Improved issue reproduction in the drop_rename test.

Ticket: ADBDEV-8908

author: bdraco
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

Saves 156 bytes of RAM and 124 bytes of flash on ESP8266 by replacing a switch statement with a linear search lookup for color mode JSON strings.

The `ColorMode` enum values are sparse bitmask combinations (1, 3, 7, 11, 19, 35, 39, 47, 55), not sequential integers. The compiler generates a large 204-byte jump table to handle all possible values up to the highest enum value.

By using parallel arrays with a simple linear search over just 9 elements, we avoid the jump table entirely. The lookup is called rarely (only when serializing light state to JSON), so the O(n) search has negligible performance impact.

Before:
```cpp
switch (mode) {
  case ColorMode::ON_OFF: return "onoff";
  case ColorMode::BRIGHTNESS: return "brightness";
  // ... generates 204-byte jump table
}
```

After:
```cpp
static constexpr ColorMode MODES[] = { ColorMode::ON_OFF, ... };  // 9 bytes
static constexpr const char *STRINGS[] = { "onoff", ... };        // 36 bytes
// Linear search over 9 elements
```

## Types of changes

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Developer breaking change (an API change that could break external components)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests
- [ ] Other

**Related issue or feature (if applicable):**

N/A - RAM/flash optimization for ESP8266

**Pull request in [esphome-docs](https://github.com/esphome/esphome-docs) with documentation (if applicable):**

N/A - no user-facing changes

## Test Environment

- [ ] ESP32
- [ ] ESP32 IDF
- [x] ESP8266
- [ ] RP2040
- [ ] BK72xx
- [ ] RTL87xx
- [ ] nRF52840

## Example entry for `config.yaml`:

```yaml

light:
  - platform: rgb
    name: "RGB Light"
    red: output_red
    green: output_green
    blue: output_blue
```

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:

## Memory Impact

|--------|--------|-------|--------|

| Flash | 500,141 bytes | 500,017 bytes | -124 bytes |

body:
## Summary

  - Made `IdSistemaInformatico` configurable via `VERIFACTU_SYSTEM_ID` environment variable
  - Removed hardcoded value from AeatClient to prevent AEAT test rejections

  ## Problem

  While testing I would clear the database multiple times and reseed it back tih this command: `php artisan migrate:fresh -- seed`.
  AEAT pre-production environment is so strict that it will reject the same invoice twice, or even create a new invoicing serie and tried again while testing, AEAT would reject invoices with the error that the same invoice with the same NIF cannot be
  declared as the first invoice when using the same  NIF  and `IdSistemaInformatico`. This prevented testing.



  ## Solution

  - Added `system_id` configuration in `config/verifactu.php` with default value '01'
  - Updated `AeatClient.php` to read from config instead of hardcoded value
  - Allows different test instances to use different system IDs via environment variables
 
 ## Benefits
  - It allows you to have multiple invoicing systems using LaravelVeriFactu package that are independent on eachother.
  
  ## Changes

  - `config/verifactu.php`: Added `system_id` config key
  - `src/Services/AeatClient.php:261`: Changed hardcoded '01' to `config('verifactu.system_id', '01')`

  ## Test plan

  - [ ] Set different `VERIFACTU_SYSTEM_ID` values in different environments
  - [ ] Verify AEAT accepts first invoices from each unique system ID
  - [ ] Confirm default value '01' is used when environment variable is not set

This implements a fix for #7315. Previously when a block was disconnected any transactions that were conflicting with transactions mined in that block were not updated to be marked as inactive.

- Introduces a generic `RecursiveUpdateTxState` function to handle recursive transaction state updates

- Adds new functional test `wallet_conflicts.py`
- Updates test expectations in `wallet_abandonconflict.py`

**Dash-specific adaptations:**
- Preserved Dash's `blockDisconnected` signature (`const CBlock& block, int height` vs Bitcoin's newer block interface)

body:
Async tools like `generate_veo_video` were timing out before completion due to hardcoded 3-minute timeout, insufficient for video generation which can take 4+ minutes.

## Changes

### Configurable timeout setting
- Added `async_tool_timeout` to Orchestration settings (60-900 seconds, default 300)
- Exposed via `asyncToolTimeout` in frontend config (milliseconds)

### Frontend polling updates
- `waitForAsyncToolResultSSE()` and `waitForAsyncToolResultPolling()` now read from `state.config.asyncToolTimeout`
- Fallback constants: `ASYNC_TOOL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS` (5 min), `ASYNC_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS` (1 min)

### Helper method
- Extracted `WP_MCP_AI_Shortcode::get_async_tool_timeout_ms()` for consistent timeout calculation across shortcode and admin test pages

```php
// Admin setting
'async_tool_timeout' => array(
    'type'    => 'number',
    'label'   => __( 'Async Tool Timeout (seconds)', 'wp-mcp-ai' ),
    'default' => 300,
    'min'     => 60,
    'max'     => 900,
),
```

```javascript
// JS uses configurable timeout with fallback
const timeout = state.config.asyncToolTimeout || ASYNC_TOOL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS;
```

author: copilot
body:
Comprehensive Dutch documentation for configuring speech language in Mapbox Navigation SDK v3 for iOS turn-by-turn navigation.

## Contents

- **Locale configuration** - Setting `NavigationRouteOptions.locale` for language selection
- **TTS configuration options** - `TTSConfig.default`, `.localOnly`, `.custom` with use cases
- **UI localization** - Banner formatters, map labels, measurement systems
- **AVSpeechSynthesizer integration** - iOS voice synthesis, Siri voice limitations
- **Supported languages table** - 27+ languages with UI/voice support status
- **Reference links** - Official Mapbox and Apple documentation

## Key Example

```swift
// Dutch navigation instructions
let routeOptions = NavigationRouteOptions(
    waypoints: waypoints, 
    locale: Locale(identifier: "nl_NL")
)
```

File: `files/Mapbox-Navigation-SDK-Spraaktaal-Configuratie.md`

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Maak van de volgende teskst een uitgebreide uitleg.
Ja, je kunt de spraaktaal van de turn-by-turn instructies in de Mapbox Navigation SDK v3 voor iOS wijzigen. Standaard worden instructies uitgesproken in de taal van de gebruikersinterface, maar je kunt dit overschrijven door de locale in te stellen bij het berekenen van de route. Dit doe je via de NavigationRouteOptions.locale property. Zo kun je bijvoorbeeld Nederlands of een andere gewenste taal instellen in plaats van Engels:

```swift
let routeOptions = NavigationRouteOptions(waypoints: waypoints, locale: Locale(identifier: "nl_NL"))
```

Als je wilt dat de instructies altijd in een specifieke taal worden uitgesproken, moet je deze locale expliciet meegeven bij het opvragen van de route. Als de gekozen taal niet wordt ondersteund door de Mapbox Voice API, zal de SDK automatisch terugvallen op AVSpeechSynthesizer (de standaard iOS spraaksynthese) om de instructies uit te spreken. Je kunt ook kiezen om altijd AVSpeechSynthesizer te gebruiken door TTSConfig.localOnly te gebruiken bij de initialisatie van de SDK, of zelfs een eigen SpeechSynthesizing implementatie aan te leveren als je volledige controle wilt over de spraakoutput, bijvoorbeeld voor een custom stem of engine zoals Siri (zie hieronder) [Spoken instructions](https://docs.mapbox.com/ios/navigation/guides/system-integration/localization-and-internationalization/#spoken-instructions).

Wat betreft het gebruik van de stem van Siri: de kennisbronnen vermelden niet expliciet dat je direct de Siri-stem kunt selecteren. Wel kun je AVSpeechSynthesizer gebruiken, en deze gebruikt de stemmen die op het apparaat beschikbaar zijn, waaronder mogelijk ook Siri-stemmen als deze door iOS worden ondersteund. Je kunt dus de lokale spraaksynthese van iOS gebruiken, maar directe ondersteuning voor het selecteren van de Siri-stem wordt niet genoemd in de documentatie. Voor volledige controle over de stem zou je een eigen SpeechSynthesizing implementatie moeten maken en deze injecteren via TTSConfig.custom [Spoken instruction override](https://docs.mapbox.com/ios/navigation/guides/turn-by-turn-navigation/user-interface/#spoken-instruction-override).

Samengevat:
- Ja, je kunt de spraaktaal wijzigen via de locale property.
- Je kunt AVSpeechSynthesizer gebruiken voor lokale stemmen, maar directe selectie van de Siri-stem wordt niet expliciet ondersteund volgens de documentatie.

Zie ook:
- [Localization and internationalization](https://docs.mapbox.com/ios/navigation/guides/system-integration/localization-and-internationalization/)
- [Spoken instructions](https://docs.mapbox.com/ios/navigation/guides/system-integration/localization-and-internationalization/#spoken-instructions)
- [Spoken instruction override](https://docs.mapbox.com/ios/navigation/guides/turn-by-turn-navigation/user-interface/#spoken-instruction-override)

The Mapbox Navigation SDK supports over a dozen major languages as well as some other locale settings. For a seamless user experience, the SDK’s default behavior matches the standard iOS behavior as much as possible, but several customization options are also available for specialized use cases.

User interface
The Mapbox Navigation SDK’s user interface automatically matches your application’s language whenever possible. To improve user experience, you should localize your application fully rather than piecemeal. If you want to display a turn-by-turn navigation experience in a language without first localizing your application, you can add the language to your Xcode project’s languages and add a stub Localizable.strings file to your application target. For more information about preparing your application for additional languages, consult “Localize your app” in Apple developer documentation.

The turn banner names the upcoming road or ramp destination in the local or national language. In some regions, the name may appear in multiple languages or scripts. A label near the bottom bar displays the current road name in the local language as well.

Distances, travel times, and arrival times are displayed according to the system language and region settings by default, regardless of the application’s language.

To override the language set the locale to the distance and time formatters:

// You need to provide the custom topBanner and bottomBanner to override the locale.

topBanner.instructionsBannerView.distanceFormatter.locale = locale
let bottomBanner = BottomBannerViewController()
bottomBanner.distanceFormatter.locale = locale
bottomBanner.dateFormatter.locale = locale

let navigationOptions = NavigationOptions(
    mapboxNavigation: mapboxNavigation,
    voiceController: mapboxNavigationProvider.routeVoiceController,
    eventsManager: mapboxNavigationProvider.eventsManager(),
    topBanner: topBanner,
    bottomBanner: bottomBanner
)

Activity Id: "" --- API Response: ----[start]---- {"name":"REDACTED","status":"Failed","startTime":"REDACTED","error":{"code":"LocationIsOfferRestricted","message":"Subscriptions are restricted from provisioning in location 'eastus'. Try again in a different location. For exceptions to this rule, see how to request a quota increase in https://aka.ms/postgres-request-quota-increase."}} -----[end]----- with azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.test, on terraform_plugin_test.tf line 40, in resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "test": 40: resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "test" { ``` To fix the issue, regions in which `azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server` configurations are available are used. While debugging the above issue, `400` error will happen during test involving `DisappearsStep` when deleted `azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_virtual_endpoint` is queried under replicated server as shown below. ``` testcase.go:173: Step 4/4 error: Error running post-apply refresh plan: exit status 1 Error: retrieving Composite Resource ID (Virtual Endpoint (Subscription: "79133cc5-0525-4c13-9cca-4298eca1d3e1" Resource Group Name: "acctest-ve-rg-251201005059771940" Flexible Server Name: "acctest-ve-primary-251201005059771940" Virtual Endpoint Name: "acctest-ve-251201005059771940") | Virtual Endpoint (Subscription: "79133cc5-0525-4c13-9cca-4298eca1d3e1" Resource Group Name: "acctest-ve-rg-251201005059771940" Flexible Server Name: "acctest-ve-replica-251201005059771940" Virtual Endpoint Name: "acctest-ve-251201005059771940")): unexpected status 400 (400 Bad Request) with error: VirtualEndpointOwnedByPrimaryServer: 'acctest-ve-replica-251201005059771940' is not a primary server. Virtual endpoints are associated to primary servers only. with azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_virtual_endpoint.test, on terraform_plugin_test.tf line 67, in resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_virtual_endpoint" "test": 67: resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_virtual_endpoint" "test" { retrieving Composite Resource ID (Virtual Endpoint (Subscription: "79133cc5-0525-4c13-9cca-4298eca1d3e1" Resource Group Name: "acctest-ve-rg-251201005059771940" Flexible Server Name: "acctest-ve-primary-251201005059771940" Virtual Endpoint Name: "acctest-ve-251201005059771940") | Virtual Endpoint (Subscription: "79133cc5-0525-4c13-9cca-4298eca1d3e1" Resource Group Name: "acctest-ve-rg-251201005059771940" Flexible Server Name: "acctest-ve-replica-251201005059771940" Virtual Endpoint Name: "acctest-ve-251201005059771940")): unexpected status 400 (400 Bad Request) with error: VirtualEndpointOwnedByPrimaryServer: 'acctest-ve-replica-251201005059771940' is not a primary server. Virtual endpoints are associated to primary servers only. panic.go:615: Error running post-test destroy, there may be dangling resources: exit status 1 ``` The error indicates that virtual endpoint is not contained under replicated server and causes the test to fail. ## Summary
This PR extracts and adds a heatwave damage/impact function module (`ImpfHeatWave`) to climada_petals. The implementation provides three different impact function factory methods:

- `from_sigmoid_function()`: Smooth sigmoid transition with configurable steepness

This commit adds comprehensive 2FA functionality to the application:

Backend:
- Add 2FA fields to users schema (twoFactorSecret, twoFactorEnabled, twoFactorBackupCodes)
- Create twoFactorAuth.ts service with TOTP generation/verification using otplib
- Add backup codes generation with bcrypt hashing for secure storage
- Implement 6 new API endpoints:
  - GET /api/auth/2fa/status - Check 2FA status
  - POST /api/auth/2fa/setup - Generate secret and QR code
  - POST /api/auth/2fa/enable - Verify code and enable 2FA
  - POST /api/auth/2fa/disable - Disable 2FA (requires password or code)
  - POST /api/auth/2fa/backup-codes/regenerate - Generate new backup codes
  - POST /api/auth/2fa/verify - Verify 2FA during login
- Modify login flow to require 2FA when enabled
- Add 2FA support for Google OAuth login flow

Frontend:
- Create TwoFactorSetup component with QR code display and backup codes management
- Add 2FA section to settings page
- Update login page with 2FA verification form
- Support both TOTP codes and backup codes for authentication

Database:
- Add migration 027_add_two_factor_auth.sql
- Create migration script scripts/run-027-2fa-migration.ts

Dependencies:
- Add otplib for TOTP generation/verification
- Add qrcode for QR code generation

To apply the database migration, run: npm run migrate:2fa

Replaces all `console.log/error/warn` calls with structured Pino logging for better observability in production.

## Changes

- **NestJS integration**: Added `nestjs-pino` with pretty-printing in dev, JSON in production
- **Services**: Replaced console calls with `Logger` from `@nestjs/common` in:
  - `auth.service.ts`, `nft.service.ts`, `effect-engine.service.ts`, `players.controller.ts`
- **Seed scripts**: Created standalone `prisma/logger.ts` for use in seed files
- **Config**: Added `LOG_LEVEL` and `NODE_ENV` to `.env.example`

## Usage

```typescript
// In NestJS services
import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common';

@Injectable()
export class MyService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(MyService.name);
  
  doSomething() {
    this.logger.log('Operation completed');
    this.logger.error('Something failed', error);
  }
}
```

```typescript
// In standalone scripts (e.g., seed files)
import logger from './logger';

logger.info('Seeding started...');
logger.error(err, 'Seeding failed');
```

author: wit765
body:
## 1. Fix bug

### 1.1 Issue

The function `doCheckGenerate` does not print the changed files as expected because the function `HashFolder` only iterate the following path: 

- `.`
- `.dockerignore`
- `.git`
- `.gitattributess `

then exits.

### 1.2 Reason

After researching, I found the reason. The parameter `exlude` passed to the `HashFolder` function contains the directory `.git`. Then, when the `filepath.WalkDir` encounters the file `.gitattributes`, it returns the error `filepath.SkipDir` because the prefix contains. `.git` .Due to encountering the error 'filepath.WalkDir' in the root directory, it immediately stopped.

### 1.3 how to fix

#### return right error

- return error`filepath.SkipDir` if it is an excluded directory
- return nil if it is an excluded file

#### handle directory `.github`

Since the directory `.github` has prefix `.git`, so we use equal to check if it is an excluded path.

## 2. Optimize code

Move 'filepath. FromSlash' from function 'HashFolder' to function 'doCheckGenerate', reducing the number of calls from 18000 to 3 times.

## 3. Fix typos

Change `exlude` to `excludes`.

_If applicable, please follow the issue templates to provide as much detail as
possible._

**Problem:**
  The web FastAPI server exposes only artifact content endpoints, so HTTP/web clients cannot read ArtifactVersion metadata that contains custom_metadata, canonical_uri, or timestamps. Features like context offloading rely on that metadata, which means the sample currently only works inside Python runners and not via the web API.

**Solution:**
Add two metadata-focused endpoints (/versions/metadata and /versions/{id}/metadata) that proxy the existing artifact-service methods, wire them into the conformance HTTP client, and add regression tests. This makes the web API feature-complete with the backend artifact service and enables context-offloading workflows over HTTP/SSE.
