author: trevor-scheer
body:
## Summary

This implements **Phase 1** of the parsing optimization strategy (as documented in [.claude/notes/PARSING_CACHE_ANALYSIS.md](.claude/notes/PARSING_CACHE_ANALYSIS.md)) by caching parsed ASTs in `DocumentIndex` and reusing them across LSP requests.

## Changes

- Add `parsed_asts` HashMap to `DocumentIndex` to cache parsed `SyntaxTree`s
- Update `update_document_index()` to parse once and cache the AST on document open/change
- Add `*_with_ast()` methods to `HoverProvider`, `CompletionProvider`, and `GotoDefinitionProvider` that accept optional cached ASTs
- Update LSP server handlers to pass file paths and use cached ASTs

## Performance Impact

### Before
Every LSP request (hover, completion, goto_definition) re-parsed the document from scratch

### After
- Parse once on document open/change events
- All subsequent requests use the cached AST
- **Expected 50-80% reduction in parsing overhead** for typical workflows

### User Experience
- Hover operations are now nearly instant (no parsing delay)
- Completion triggers during typing are significantly faster
- Goto definition responds more quickly

## Technical Details

The implementation uses `Arc<apollo_parser::SyntaxTree>` for efficient sharing of parsed ASTs across threads. The cache is invalidated and updated automatically on document changes through the existing `update_document_index` flow.

Key optimization locations:
- [hover.rs](crates/graphql-project/src/hover.rs#L91-L106) - Uses cached AST, falls back to parsing
- [completion.rs](crates/graphql-project/src/completion.rs#L112-L128) - Uses cached AST
- [goto_definition.rs](crates/graphql-project/src/goto_definition.rs#L55-L77) - Uses cached AST
- [project.rs](crates/graphql-project/src/project.rs#L175-L198) - Parses and caches on document update

## What's Not Yet Optimized

`find_references` still parses all workspace documents on each request. This is the biggest remaining bottleneck and will be addressed in Phase 2 (batch parsing optimization).

## Testing

- ✅ All tests pass (`cargo test`)
- ✅ Code compiles successfully (`cargo check`)
- ✅ Clippy lints pass (`cargo clippy`)
- ✅ Format check passes (`cargo fmt -- --check`)

1. **Product Analytics Events**: Added privacy-compliant analytics events for capture (`item_capture_started`, `item_capture_cancelled`), creation (`item_created`, `item_creation_failed`), editing (`item_edited`, `item_edit_cancelled`, `item_edit_failed`), deletion (`item_deleted`, `item_deletion_failed`), and search (`item_search_used`). All events follow snake_case property naming conventions and exclude PII, using only counts, booleans, and enums.

2. **Feature Flags**: Implemented `wardrobe_image_cleanup_enabled` and `wardrobe_ai_attributes_enabled` flags with server-side authoritative evaluation. Safe defaults (false) are used when the flag service is unreachable. Client-side hooks (`useWardrobeFeatureFlags`) adjust UI visibility based on flag state.

3. **Structured Logging & Correlation IDs**: Added `structuredLogger.ts` for consistent JSON logging across edge functions with environment tagging. Correlation IDs are generated client-side and propagated via `X-Correlation-ID` header for end-to-end request tracing.

4. **EXIF Privacy Protection**: Client-side EXIF stripping is enforced in `imageUpload.ts` via expo-image-manipulator regardless of feature flag state, ensuring location and device metadata are never uploaded.

5. **Edge Function Updates**: Updated `delete-wardrobe-item`, `process-item-image`, `detect-item-attributes`, and `get-feature-flags` functions with structured logging, correlation ID support, and proper error classification.

author: bug-ops
body:
## Summary

Implements a complete **Spaced Repetition learning system** using the **FSRS 5.2 algorithm** (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler). This foundation enables intelligent review scheduling based on cognitive science principles, optimizing long-term retention of Helix keybindings.

### Key Features

- **Performance Tracking**: Records command attempts with timing, success rate, and FSRS state (stability, difficulty, mastery level)
- **Intelligent Scheduling**: Priority-based review queue that prioritizes harder commands and overdue items
- **Learning Analytics**: Mastery distribution, progress tracking, and plateau detection
- **Review Sessions**: Complete workflow for practicing due reviews with automatic mastery progression tracking

### Implementation Details

**FSRS 5.2 Integration**:
- ML-trained algorithm (350M+ reviews dataset)
- 99.6% better prediction accuracy than SM-2
- 20-30% fewer reviews needed for same retention

**Architecture**:
- 4 new modules: `performance`, `scheduler`, `analytics`, `session`
- Shared ownership pattern: `Rc<RefCell<PerformanceTracker>>`
- Single-threaded design (TUI-appropriate)

**Mastery Levels** (4 tiers):
- Beginner: New or Learning state
- Intermediate: Review state, stability < 7 days
- Advanced: Review state, stability 7-30 days  
- Master: Review state, stability > 30 days, difficulty < 5

**Priority Formula**:
```
urgency = days_overdue / scheduled_days
difficulty_weight = difficulty / 5.0
priority = urgency × difficulty_weight
```

### Quality Metrics

✅ **287 tests passing** (250 lib + 37 integration/doctests)  
✅ **Zero clippy warnings** (`--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`)  
✅ **Security audit**: APPROVED (low risk dependencies)  
✅ **Performance review**: Grade A+ (excellent design)  
✅ **Code review**: APPROVED (idiomatic Rust, clean architecture)

### Test Coverage

- **51 unit tests** across 4 modules (performance, scheduler, analytics, session)
- **7 integration tests** covering full workflows
- **12 doctests** for API documentation

### Files Changed

```
10 files changed, 5,627 insertions(+), 498 deletions(-)

New modules:
- src/learning/performance.rs   (508 lines) - PerformanceTracker + FSRS
- src/learning/scheduler.rs     (314 lines) - Scheduler + priority queue
- src/learning/analytics.rs     (444 lines) - Analytics + insights
- src/learning/session.rs       (459 lines) - ReviewSession workflow
- src/learning/mod.rs           (32 lines)  - Public API exports
- tests/spaced_repetition.rs    (345 lines) - Integration tests
```

### Usage Example

```rust
use helix_trainer::learning::{PerformanceTracker, Scheduler, ReviewSession, Analytics};
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::cell::RefCell;

// 1. Create tracker
let tracker = Rc::new(RefCell::new(PerformanceTracker::new()));

// 2. Record practice
tracker.borrow_mut().record_attempt(
    "dd",
    Duration::from_secs(2),
    true,  // success
    Duration::from_secs(1),  // optimal_time
);

// 3. Schedule reviews
let scheduler = Scheduler::new(Rc::clone(&tracker));
let due_reviews = scheduler.get_due_reviews();

// 4. Run session
let mut session = ReviewSession::new(&scheduler, Rc::clone(&tracker), 10);
while let Some(item) = session.current_item() {
    session.record_and_next(duration, success, optimal_time);
}

// 5. Check analytics
let analytics = Analytics::new(Rc::clone(&tracker));
let summary = analytics.get_mastery_summary();
```

### Dependencies Added

```toml
chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
fsrs = "5.2"
```

### What's NOT Included (UI Integration - Next Phase)

This is a **foundational library**. UI integration will follow in separate PRs:

- [ ] Menu items ("Review Commands", "View Progress", "Statistics")
- [ ] Review screen UI
- [ ] Statistics screen UI  
- [ ] Data persistence (save/load from JSON)
- [ ] Integration with existing GameSession

### References

- **FSRS crate**: https://crates.io/crates/fsrs/5.2.0
- **FSRS algorithm**: https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs4anki/wiki
- **Planning docs**: `.local/plans/phase1/02-spaced-repetition/`

author: imichaelmoore
body:
`slurp()` uses `stat()` before `open()`, creating a race window where file size can change between the stat and read calls:

- If the file shrinks, the buffer may contain uninitialized data
- If it grows, data is truncated

**Fix:** Use `fstat()` on the open file descriptor instead.

author: imichaelmoore
body:
`fpath()` returns `NULL` when the combined directory + filename exceeds `PATH_MAX`. Both call sites pass the result directly to other functions without checking:

- `hash_deps()` passes it to `slurp()`
- `dep_monitor()` passes it to `inotify_add_watch()`

This causes a NULL pointer dereference if a job has a long directory path combined with a long dependency filename.

**Fix:** Check for NULL before use and log an appropriate error message.

Child process output is forwarded to syslog without sanitization. A malicious or compromised child process could inject:

- Terminal escape sequences
- Fake log entries that look like they came from other processes
- Characters that confuse log parsers

**Fix:** Add `sanitize_log()` function that replaces control characters (except `\n` and `\t`) with `?` before logging.

author: imichaelmoore
body:
Several issues in `slurp()`:

1. **No size limit** - A large dependency file could exhaust memory
2. **Partial reads** - `read()` can return fewer bytes than requested; the code treated this as an error
3. **EINTR** - Interrupted system calls weren't retried

**Fix:**
- Add 10MB size limit (`SLURP_MAX_SIZE`)
- Read in a loop until all bytes are received
- Retry on `EINTR`
- Log malloc failures

`putenv()` stores the pointer directly into the environment without copying. The strings come from the config parser's token storage. If `execv()` fails and the child continues to the error handling path, the environment contains pointers to memory that may be in an inconsistent state.

   - No unit tests to verify behavior

Implements dashboard generation from captured metrics data (from `capture-metrics.py`) to enable visual analysis of agent activity, performance trends, and system health.

## Changes

**Core Script** (`ops/scripts/generate-dashboard.py`)
- Generates three dashboard types: summary (overview + top agents), detail (per-agent breakdowns), trends (historical timelines)
- ASCII bar charts with Unicode blocks for visual representation
- Handles missing data, invalid JSON, empty metrics gracefully
- Pure Python stdlib, no external dependencies

**Testing** (`ops/scripts/test-generate-dashboard.sh`)
- 10 test cases covering generation, output formats, error handling
- Validates dashboard structure and chart rendering

**Documentation**
- `ops/README.md`: Integration documentation with dashboard type descriptions
- `ops/scripts/DASHBOARD_USAGE_EXAMPLES.md`: Workflow examples and troubleshooting

**Sample Output** (`work/reports/dashboards/`)
- Three dashboard markdown files demonstrating each type

## Usage

```bash
# Complete workflow
python3 ops/scripts/capture-metrics.py --output-file metrics.json
python3 ops/scripts/generate-dashboard.py --input metrics.json

# Single dashboard to stdout
python3 ops/scripts/generate-dashboard.py --dashboard-type summary --output-file -

# Update existing
python3 ops/scripts/generate-dashboard.py --update --verbose
```

Dashboard types support `summary` (top agents + recent activity), `detail` (per-agent metrics), `trends` (historical analysis), or `all` (default).

Implementación de mejoras en autenticación, notificaciones por email y endpoints de consulta. author: ingcristhian
body:
## 🚀 Release: Product Catalog MVP

Despliegue del MVP del catálogo de productos a producción.

## ✨ Features Incluidas

### Core Functionality
- ✅ Catálogo público de productos con paginación
- ✅ Búsqueda de productos por nombre/descripción
- ✅ Página de detalle de producto
- ✅ Integración con WhatsApp para consultas
- ✅ Carrito de compras (localStorage)
- ✅ Diseño responsive con Bootstrap 5.3

### Arquitectura MVC
- ✅ **Modelo**: `Producto.php` con acceso READ-ONLY a BD compartida
- ✅ **Controlador**: `ProductoController.php` para catálogo y detalles
- ✅ **Vistas**: Layout principal, catálogo, detalle, error 404

### Seguridad
- ✅ Prepared statements (prevención SQL injection)
- ✅ Sanitización de outputs (prevención XSS)
- ✅ Usuario de BD con permisos READ-ONLY para productos
- ✅ CSRF tokens ready

### Frontend
- ✅ CSS personalizado con animaciones
- ✅ JavaScript para gestión de carrito
- ✅ Bootstrap 5.3 + Bootstrap Icons
- ✅ Lazy loading de imágenes

## 🔧 Cambios Técnicos

### Commits incluidos:
- `f5d733f` - fix: update workflow secrets naming convention
- `60fea32` - feat: implement product catalog MVP
- `0771e30` - feat: initial project structure for KyoShop Store

### Configuración
- ✅ GitHub Actions para deploy automático
- ✅ Workflows configurados para dev y producción
- ✅ Secrets de GitHub configurados

## 📋 Pre-Deploy Checklist

- [x] Código probado en desarrollo (`dev.kyoshop.co`)
- [x] Secrets de producción configurados
- [x] Base de datos compartida configurada
- [x] Usuario READ-ONLY de BD creado
- [x] Workflows actualizados

## 🗄️ Requisitos de Base de Datos

La aplicación espera que exista la tabla `productos` en la base de datos `kyosankk_inventory` (compartida con el sistema admin).

**Estructura mínima esperada:**
```sql
productos (
  id, codigo, nombre, descripcion, 
  precio, stock, imagen, categoria_id, 
  activo, fecha_creacion
)
```

## 🌐 URLs

- **Producción**: https://kyoshop.co
- **Desarrollo**: https://dev.kyoshop.co (✅ verificado)

## 📝 Próximos Pasos

Después de este deploy:
- [ ] Verificar funcionamiento en producción
- [ ] Implementar página de carrito
- [ ] Implementar checkout con ePayco
- [ ] Implementar gestión de pedidos

## ⚠️ Notas Importantes

- Este es el **primer deploy a producción**
- La tienda mostrará productos en tiempo real desde la BD compartida
- Cualquier cambio en productos desde el admin se reflejará automáticamente
- El carrito funciona con localStorage (no persiste entre dispositivos)

Resolves session stack tracking for improved workflow efficiency.

author: soderlind
body:
This pull request introduces version 1.0.1 of the AI Alt Text plugin, focusing on enhancing user experience by adding "Generate with AI" buttons to the WordPress media library. These buttons allow users to generate alt text for images directly from both the single media edit page and the media library grid view modal. The update also improves button placement and styling to better integrate with the WordPress admin interface.

**New AI Alt Text Generation Buttons:**

* Added a "Generate with AI" button below the alt text field on the single media edit page, left-aligned for consistency with the WordPress UI.
* Added a "Generate with AI" button below the alt text field in the media library grid view modal, right-aligned and styled using WordPress's native `copy-to-clipboard-container` class.

**Styling and Integration Improvements:**

* Improved the placement and styling of the new buttons using WordPress native styling, ensuring a seamless appearance in both the single edit and grid modal contexts.

**Technical and Versioning Updates:**

* Bumped the plugin version to 1.0.1 in `ai-alt-text.php`, `package.json`, and `readme.txt`, and added new constants for version, path, and URL. This PR refactors the Skills Exercised (Chronologically) logic out of inspect_db.py into a dedicated module, skill_timeline.py.
Previously, the skills timeline query, grouping, and formatting lived directly inside inspect_db.py, which made the file less readable and added extra responsibility to a script meant mainly for manual database inspection. This refactor improves separation of concerns by moving all skills-timeline–specific logic into its own file, while inspect_db.py now simply calls into the module when generating output.

The new skill_timeline.py module handles:

- Querying skill, project, and timestamp data
- Grouping entries by skill name
- Ordering occurrences chronologically per skill
- Printing a clean, readable, bullet-style timeline

The output format remains the same as the previously improved version, with skills grouped under a single header and chronological entries listed below each skill. To support this change, a new unit test file (test_skill_timeline.py) was added, using mocked database interactions to verify grouping and output without relying on the actual database.
Overall, this change improves code organization, readability, and testability without modifying existing behavior.

## Summary

- new flags/defaults: `FEATURE_PASSKEYS_ENABLED`, `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID`, `WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME`, `WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN`, `WEBAUTHN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WEBAUTHN_CHALLENGE_TTL_MS`

author: copilot
body:
Implements backend infrastructure for store owners to manage internal team members with role-based access to the seller panel. This is Phase 2 functionality per the issue requirements.

## Domain Model

- **`StoreRole`** enum: `StoreOwner`, `CatalogManager`, `OrderManager`, `ReadOnly`
- **`StoreUserStatus`** enum: `Pending`, `Active`, `Deactivated`
- **`StoreUser`** entity: Links IdentityUser to stores with assigned roles, tracks invitation state and audit fields

## Application Layer

- `IStoreUserService` / `IStoreUserRepository` interfaces
- Command/Result pattern for: `InviteStoreUser`, `AcceptStoreUserInvitation`, `UpdateStoreUserRole`, `DeactivateStoreUser`

## Infrastructure

- `StoreUserService` with:
  - Cryptographically secure invitation tokens (7-day expiry)
  - Email normalization to prevent case-based duplicates
  - Protection against removing/demoting the only store owner
- `StoreUserRepository` with EF Core implementation
- `SellerDbContext` updated with entity configuration and indexes

## Usage

```csharp
// Invite a user
var result = await _storeUserService.InviteUserAsync(new InviteStoreUserCommand
{
    StoreId = storeId,
    Email = "team@example.com",
    Role = StoreRole.CatalogManager,
    InvitedBy = currentUserId
});

// Check access
bool hasAccess = await _storeUserService.HasStoreAccessAsync(storeId, userId);
StoreRole? role = await _storeUserService.GetUserRoleAsync(storeId, userId);
```

## Tests

26 unit tests added covering invitation flow, role updates, deactivation, and edge cases (expired tokens, only-owner protection, etc.). All 307 solution tests pass.

> ## User Story
> As a store owner I want to manage internal users and their roles so that my team members can work in the seller panel with appropriate permissions.
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - Given I am a store owner, when I open the user management section, then I can see a list of internal users associated with my store including their roles and status.
> - Given I am a store owner, when I invite a new internal user by email and assign a role, then the system sends an invitation and creates a pending user record.
> - Given an invited internal user receives an invitation, when they accept the invitation and complete registration, then they gain access to the seller panel with the assigned role.
> - Given I am a store owner, when I change the role of an existing internal user, then their permissions in the seller panel are updated accordingly on their next action or session.
> - Given I am a store owner, when I deactivate an internal user, then that user can no longer sign in to the seller panel for my store and any active sessions are invalidated.
> 
> ## Notes
> - At minimum define roles such as StoreOwner (full access), CatalogManager (product management), OrderManager (order processing) and ReadOnly/Accounting (report access).

body:
Comprehensive upgrade adding dynamic pair filtering, a new momentum strategy, portfolio-level risk management, and improved API reliability for 2025.

## Dynamic Pair Scanning
- Added slippage estimation via orderbook depth analysis
- Pairs filtered by `max_slippage_pct` (default 0.5%) and `min_liquidity_depth` 
- Updated scoring weights: volume 15%, spread 20%, volatility 20%, funding 10%, fee 15%, **slippage 20%**

## Momentum Strategy
New strategy combining multiple momentum signals:
```python
MomentumStrategy({
    "roc_period": 10,      # Rate of change
    "rsi_period": 14,      # RSI confirmation
    "momentum_threshold": 0.02,
})
```
Regime detector updated to allocate weights to momentum (30% in trending, 30% in high volatility regimes).

## Portfolio-Level Risk Controls
- `portfolio_stop_loss_pct`: Hard stop on total portfolio loss
- `portfolio_take_profit_pct`: Optional profit-taking threshold
- `trailing_stop_pct`: Trailing stop from peak value
- **Safe mode**: Auto-triggers at 15% drawdown or 5% daily loss, reducing position sizes 50% and blocking new trades

```python
rm.check_portfolio_limits()  # Returns (should_continue, action, reasons)
rm.get_position_adjustments(positions, prices)  # Returns close/reduce actions
rm.apply_safe_mode()  # Returns adjusted risk params when in safe mode
```

## Enhanced Reliability
- Smart retry with rate-limit detection (`429xxx` codes) and timeout handling
- Jitter to prevent thundering herd
- `APIMetrics` dataclass tracking success rates, latency, rate limits
- Prometheus-compatible metrics export via `MonitoringMetrics.to_prometheus_format()`

## API Updates
- Updated to KuCoin API v3 authentication
- Session timeout configuration (30s total, 10s connect)

body:
##  CLI Provider Authentication Support for STACKIT SDK

### Summary

This PR adds comprehensive support for using STACKIT CLI provider credentials directly in the SDK, enabling seamless authentication across CLI and SDK-based tools without requiring re-authentication. (requires https://github.com/stackitcloud/stackit-cli/pull/1130)

#### Key Features

- **CLI Credential Integration**: New `cliauth` package enables SDK applications to read and use credentials stored by the STACKIT CLI
- **Automatic Token Refresh**: Built-in OAuth2 token refresh with bidirectional sync (tokens refreshed by SDK are written back to storage)
- **Multi-Profile Support**: Full support for CLI profiles with automatic resolution from explicit parameters, environment variables, or config files
- **Cross-Platform Storage**: Credentials stored in system keyring (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, Windows Credential Manager) with automatic file fallback
- **Thread-Safe**: Concurrent request handling with automatic token refresh coordination
- **Background Refresh**: Optional background goroutine for proactive token refresh before expiration

#### Architecture

The implementation consists of four logical commits:

1. **Core Authentication Package** (`core/cliauth`):
   - `credentials.go`: Credential reading from keyring/file with profile resolution
   - `token_refresh.go`: OAuth2 token refresh with configurable endpoints
   - `flow.go`: Thread-safe `http.RoundTripper` implementation for automatic auth injection
   - `background_refresh.go`: Background token refresh with context-based lifecycle
   - `doc.go`: Comprehensive package documentation with usage examples

2. **SDK Configuration Integration** (`core/config/cli_auth.go`):
   - `WithCLIProviderAuth(profile)`: Configure SDK clients to use CLI credentials
   - `WithCLIBackgroundTokenRefresh(ctx)`: Enable background token refresh


#### Usage Example

```go
// Basic usage with default profile
client, err := dns.NewAPIClient(
    config.WithCLIProviderAuth(""),
)

// With custom profile
client, err := dns.NewAPIClient(
    config.WithCLIProviderAuth("production"),
)

// With background token refresh
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()

client, err := dns.NewAPIClient(
    config.WithCLIBackgroundTokenRefresh(ctx),
    config.WithCLIProviderAuth(""),
)
```

#### Storage Locations

**System Keyring (preferred):**
- Service name: `stackit-cli-api` (default) or `stackit-cli-api/{profile}`
- Platforms: macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, Windows Credential Manager

**File Fallback:**
- Default profile: `~/.stackit/cli-api-auth-storage.txt`
- Custom profiles: `~/.stackit/profiles/{profile}/cli-api-auth-storage.txt`
- Format: Base64-encoded JSON

#### Profile Resolution Order

1. Explicit profile parameter
2. `STACKIT_CLI_PROFILE` environment variable
3. `~/.config/stackit/cli-profile.txt` config file
4. `"default"` fallback

#### Backward Compatibility

- compatible with credentials created by existing STACKIT CLI versions
- All file paths, formats, and keyring service names match CLI exactly
- Users can seamlessly switch between CLI and SDK-based tools

#### Related Issues

* **requires**: https://github.com/stackitcloud/stackit-cli/pull/1130 for cli-support
* Partially fixes: https://github.com/stackitcloud/terraform-provider-stackit/issues/719
* RFC: https://github.com/stackitcloud/terraform-provider-stackit/discussions/880


## Checklist

- [x] Issue was linked above
- [x] **No generated code was adjusted manually** (check [comments in file header](https://github.com/stackitcloud/stackit-sdk-go/blob/783b7fa78e41d072a3ff08e246a13f1bef5aa764/services/dns/api_default.go#L9))
- [x] Changelogs

    - [x] Changelog(s) of the service(s) were adjusted (see e.g. [here](https://github.com/stackitcloud/stackit-sdk-go/blob/f1e375a38064f798821d22a951bc74ca8a9c8845/services/dns/CHANGELOG.md))

- [x] Unit tests got implemented or updated

**Fixes map recentering unexpectedly on user/default location**

Related to #212

The issue was caused by two problems:
1. **Camera recenter loop**: the map was re-centered on `userLocation` every time it updated, breaking user interactions
2. **Query restart**: the geo query was re-launched repeatedly instead of only once at startup

**Solution:**
- Added `isCameraCentered` flag to ensure camera centers on `userLocation` only once at startup
- Applied the same logic to the geo query so it starts only once
- Introduced a `DisposableEffect` to keep user location updated in real time without forcing recenter

Tests / validation:
- Map no longer resets when interacting after initial load
- Query runs once and continues to deliver updates
- User location updates smoothly without breaking camera state

No impact on public API – only internal map behavior adjusted.
